messages.subject: Issues with SEM Model Fit
parts:
Hello lavaan community,

I am currently working on a structural equation model (SEM) using the lavaan package in R and have encountered some challenges with the model fit. I would greatly appreciate your insights on the following:
 I am testing a conceptual model that includes latent variables representing gait quality, physical activity, pain, cognition, depression, and inflammation. The paths and latent variable definitions are specified in the lavaan syntax as follows:

  # Paths
  Falls ~ Gaitqualitylatent + PAlatent + Pain
  Gaitqualitylatent ~ Cognitionlatent + PAlatent + Pain
  PAlatent ~ Cognitionlatent + Depression + Pain
  Cognitionlatent ~ Depression + Inflammation
  Depression ~ Pain
  Inflammation ~ Pain

  # Additional term
  PAlatent ~~ 1 * PAlatent

  # Latent variable definitions
  Gaitqualitylatent =~ avg_step_regularity + avg_stride_regularity + avg_step_time_variability_mode + avg_usual_speed
  PAlatent =~ avg_step_count + avg_run_duration_min + total_MET_minutes
  Cognitionlatent =~ reaction_time + pairs_matching

When I run the SEM model, I receive output with estimates, but the standard errors and p-values are not provided for the parameters. Here is a snippet of the output:

Parameter Estimates:

Standard errors                             Standard
Information                                 Expected
Information saturated (h1) model          Structured

Latent Variables:
                       Estimate     Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
  Gaitqualitylatent =~                                      
    avg_stp_rglrty           1.000                          
    avg_strd_rglrt           1.178       NA                  
    avg_stp_tm_vr_          -0.365       NA                  
    avg_usual_sped          80.245       NA                  
  PAlatent =~                                                
    avg_step_count           1.000                          
    avg_rn_drtn_mn          15.586       NA                  
    total_MET_mnts           2.016       NA                  
  Cognitionlatent =~                                        
    reaction_time            1.000                          
    pairs_matching           0.003       NA     

   I am seeking guidance on why the standard errors and p-values are not provided for the parameters. Are there specific issues with my model specification or data that I should address?

 
install.packages("lavaan")
library(lavaan)


data <- read.csv(data)

# Fit the model
fit <- sem(model, data = data, optim.method = "NLMINB")

# Display the summary
summary(fit)

I would be grateful for any advice or suggestions you may have to help resolve this issue. Thank you for your time and assistance!

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Issues with SEM Model Fit
parts:
Your model is not identified.

Identification can be associated with the model (as in, this model will never be identified) or a feature of the model with the data (this model is not identified, with this data).

One way to find out the problem is to start small, and then add to the model and see where it fails.

For example, I would start with:

Gaitqualitylatent =~ avg_step_regularity + avg_stride_regularity + avg_step_time_variability_mode + avg_usual_speed
  PAlatent =~ avg_step_count + avg_run_duration_min + total_MET_minutes
  Cognitionlatent =~ reaction_time + pairs_matching

And see if this is identified or has any problems, then add variables one at a time.


Another thing to do is look at the parameters, and see which ones are not values you might expect. This can indicate a problem.

For example:

Cognitionlatent =~                                        
    reaction_time            1.000                          
    pairs_matching           0.003       NA

Suggests to me that reaction_time and pairs_matching are not correlated - if this is the case, they shouldn't be the indicators of a latent factor (it might not be the case - this result could have happened because of problems in other parts of the model).

Also, is this line necessary?

# Additional term
  PAlatent ~~ 1 * PAlatent
Jeremy

I agree that your identification problem is in the factor structure. Your common factors all covary with other variables in the model--the structural model is nearly saturated--and you have no free residual covariancea and no cross-loadings. So the relevant identification rule is probably the two indicator rule. This says that identification is achieved if each common factor has at least two indicators with strong loadings and the factor has a strong covariance with something else.
     Looking at the estimated loadings, I think the problem is that you do not have two indicators with strong loadings for each common factors. The solution may not be converged, but as it stands, you have loadings near 0 and other loadings with wildly improbable values.
     I suggest that you calculate a correlation matrix for the indicators and check whether you have strong correlations among all of the indicators for each common factor. Also check to see whether correlations among indicators of the same factor are higher than correlations among indicators of different factors.

  Gaitqualitylatent ~ Cognitionlatent + PAlatent + Pain
  PAlatent ~ Cognitionlatent + Depression + Pain
  Cognitionlatent ~ Depression + Inflammation
  Depression ~ Pain
  Inflammation ~ Pain

  # Additional term
  PAlatent ~~ 1 * PAlatent

  # Latent variable definitions

I was about to say what Ed said, but less eloquently. :) 

One more thing. You say " latent variable definitions seem reasonable." The joy, and the pain, of SEM analysis is that our theories seem reasonable, but when we test them (rigorously) with SEM, it's a  rude awakening and we discover that the data says that are definitions (and hence our theories) are not at all reasonable.

Jeremy
